scenario.summary: ErrTraffic is a Malware-as-a-Service framework that compromises WordPress sites to inject malicious JavaScript and deliver 'ClickFix' social engineering lures. It utilizes 'EtherHiding' by querying Polygon blockchain smart contracts for resilient C2 infrastructure resolution and tricks users into running PowerShell commands that download infostealers like Vidar and Stealc.

meta.rationale: Scoping targets known WordPress servers for the distribution side. Resolution checks apply fleet-wide as any host can be a victim of malvertising or ClickFix lures.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary has compromised internal WordPress servers to host backdoors, or internal clients are interacting with ClickFix lures that resolve C2 infrastructure via blockchain RPC endpoints (EtherHiding).

hunt.name: ErrTraffic: Web Compromise and Blockchain Resolution
hunt.description: This hunt targets the dual nature of ErrTraffic: the server-side compromise of WordPress infrastructure for payload hosting and the client-side use of EtherHiding (blockchain-based dead drop resolvers) to identify rotated C2 domains. It identifies vulnerable WordPress assets, monitors for unauthorized PHP modifications, and identifies anomalous client traffic to blockchain RPC providers and suspicious TLDs like .beer and .cfd.

config.content: SELECT DISTINCT device_hostname, package_name, package_version FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%wordpress%'
config.description: Find hosts running WordPress to narrow the scope for server-side compromise indicators.
config.expected_signal: A list of hosts with WordPress. Silence indicates no WordPress detected in inventory, shifting focus to client-side lure interaction.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, file_path, process_name, actor_user_name, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE (LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%/index.php' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%/wp-content/plugins/%') AND activity_id IN (1, 3, 4, 99) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Detect the deployment of PHP backdoors (e.g., inside index.php or plugin directories) on servers identified in the scoping step.
config.expected_signal: File writes or modifications to core WordPress files. Correlating these hits with non-admin accounts or unusual processes indicates compromise.

config.content: SELECT query_hostname, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE (LOWER(query_hostname) LIKE '%.beer' OR LOWER(query_hostname) LIKE '%.cfd' OR LOWER(query_hostname) LIKE '%.club' OR LOWER(query_hostname) LIKE '%.click' OR LOWER(query_hostname) LIKE '%.cyou' OR LOWER(query_hostname) LIKE '%.lat' OR LOWER(query_hostname) LIKE '%.sbs' OR LOWER(query_hostname) LIKE '%.shop' OR LOWER(query_hostname) LIKE '%.xyz') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY query_hostname
config.description: Stack-count unusual TLDs to separate standard web browsing from rare, campaign-specific C2 infrastructure.
config.expected_signal: Rare DNS queries to domains in the specified TLDs. Legitimate domains will be common; malicious C2s used in rotation will be unique to a few hosts.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, query_hostname, time FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE (LOWER(query_hostname) LIKE '%quiknode.pro' OR LOWER(query_hostname) LIKE '%polygon-rpc.com' OR LOWER(query_hostname) LIKE '%quicknode.com') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
